lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality.
items.because: Those details do not help readers assess the qualifications shown and draw attention away from relevant experience and skills.

items.says: Experience appears after Education.
items.because: Readers reach the work history and product transition only after both degrees.

items.says: The Experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: Crestline appears above the more recent Harbor internship, delaying the more product-aligned experience.

items.says: The bullet presents a calculation change as a reduction in late deliveries.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments can lower the reported rate without making any shipments less late.

items.says: The bullet uses the first-person pronoun “my.”
items.because: It breaks the résumé’s phrase-style convention.

items.says: The 30% reduction has no comparison period or starting rate.
items.because: Without a comparison point, readers cannot judge the scale or context of the change.

items.says: Passive wording obscures who rolled out the redesign and who received training.
items.because: The phrasing makes the candidate’s contribution and the rollout harder to assess.

items.says: The forecast-error reduction is buried after the review scope and duration.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the key result only at the end.

items.says: The bullet attributes the conversion increase to the flow change without saying how that effect was established.
items.because: A before-and-after change alone cannot show that the new flow caused the increase.

items.says: “By 35%” does not say whether the change is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the figure measures.

items.says: The self-service feature has a delivery-timing result but no post-launch outcome.
items.because: Shipping early does not show whether the feature improved dispute handling or another user or business result.

items.says: The shipping result is delayed until the end of the bullet.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the two-weeks-ahead outcome.

items.says: The roadmap impact is buried after the research methods and estimate.
items.because: The business-case result is the clearest account of why the work mattered.

items.says: “1.1 million dollars” is wordy.
items.because: A compact numeric amount and currency symbol would take less space.

items.says: The opt-in comparison does not, by itself, isolate the redesign’s effect.
items.because: Merchants who opt in may differ in ways that also affect onboarding outcomes.

items.says: The bullet does not establish that the 9 tonnes of food would otherwise have been discarded.
items.because: Redistribution through the app does not show what would have happened to the food without it.

items.says: The bullet does not say what product or rollout work the candidate personally did.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the Product Lead contribution involved.

items.says: The pickup-slot and staff-cover-shift figures are not clearly defined or comparable.
items.because: The bullet gives neither consistent definitions nor the periods covered by the figures.

items.says: The working-sessions bullet gives no outcome from the scheduling work.
items.because: It shows participation but not what changed or why the work mattered.

items.says: The bullet does not quantify how much the intake form was shortened or what effect that had.
items.because: Four clinics shows reach, not the result of the work.

items.says: Passive phrasing obscures the candidate’s role in mapping intake and changing the form.
items.because: Readers cannot tell who performed those actions.

items.says: The adoption result is delayed until after the methods.
items.because: Readers reach the outcome more slowly.

items.says: The practicum repeats the Harbor Payments onboarding result.
items.because: The two bullets describe the same achievement.

items.says: The practicum attributes a merchant-onboarding result to a hospital-network project.
items.because: The result appears under the later Harbor internship and does not fit the practicum’s hospital work.
